subject.title: [Bug]: childless codex-native subagent stuck initializing can exhaust unified exec capacity

question: Should OpenClaw warn, status-query, or terminalize childless Codex-native subagents stuck in initializing before the current 30-minute native-subagent grace, and what threshold should apply?
rationale: The remaining gap is real in source, but choosing an earlier warning versus automatic loss changes how OpenClaw treats quiet native Codex subagents that may still be valid.

options.title: Add early warning or status-query recovery
options.body: Surface stuck childless Codex-native initialization around 5-10 minutes and try a Codex state/transcript recovery path before marking the task lost.

options.title: Shorten init-only terminalization
options.body: Mark childless Codex-native tasks lost earlier only while they remain in initialization, accepting the risk of false terminalization for quiet valid work.

options.title: Keep 30-minute fallback and split diagnostics
options.body: Leave recovery timing unchanged and track embedded Codex version/status and gateway restart improvements separately.

recommendation.title: Add early warning or status-query recovery
recommendation.body: Surface stuck childless Codex-native initialization around 5-10 minutes and try a Codex state/transcript recovery path before marking the task lost.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent work on blocked Codex-native spawn terminalization makes this the closest current history signal for the recovery-policy choice.
